title: Kerberoasting
overview: Correlate service-ticket requests for distinct services alongside encryption and requester context.
prerequisites: Be comfortable reading timestamps and windows security or sysmon projection fields.

attack.name: Kerberoasting
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: Three distinct legacy-encrypted service tickets requested by one user during ten minutes warrant investigation.
evidence: Check event 4769, encryption type, requesting identity and the distinct service names.
false_positive: Legacy services and trusted inventory jobs can produce bursts of service-ticket requests.
tuning: Baseline service accounts, isolate legacy protocols and verify ownership before excluding a workload.
response: Review requester activity and service-account exposure. Move accounts to managed credentials according to policy.
prevention: Prefer gMSAs and modern encryption. Audit service principal assignments and legacy-client dependencies.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The exercise checks request metadata only, with no ticket capture or password recovery.

options: Distinct service targets and legacy encryption
questions.explanation: The rule combines a cryptographic property and distinct services per user.

options: Use managed service accounts and modern encryption
